title: NY State Assembly · District 28
area: Central Queens, including Forest Hills, Rego Park and Kew Gardens.

context.text: Incumbent Andrew Hevesi defeated Jonathan Rinaldi 87.7%-11.8% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Rinaldi remains on the November general-election ballot on the minor No Kings Party line; David Kemp, who withdrew from the Republican primary, is on the ballot on the 4 Our Immigrants Party line. The Working Families Party primary was canceled after Hevesi withdrew from that line.

On June 24, 2026, Rinaldi was arrested and arraigned on nearly 20 counts of fraud related to his 2025 New York City Council campaign, in which prosecutors say he used AI-generated content, including fabricated endorsements and deepfake videos of opponents.

summary.text: Andrew Hevesi is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 28 in Queens, first elected in a May 2005 special election. A lifelong resident of the area, he previously worked as a chief of staff and as Director of Community Affairs for the New York City Public Advocate. He chairs the Children and Families Committee and won the June 2026 Democratic primary against Jonathan Rinaldi with 87.7% of the vote.

background.text: According to his official Assembly biography, he is a lifelong resident of the area he represents, which includes Forest Hills, Rego Park, Ridgewood, Richmond Hill, Middle Village, Glendale and Kew Gardens.
Earned a B.A. in political science from Queens College.
Served as Chief of Staff for Jeff Klein and worked as Director of Community Affairs for the New York City Public Advocate before being elected to the Assembly, according to Ballotpedia.
First elected to the 28th Assembly District on May 10, 2005.
Chaired the Assembly Social Services Committee from 2015 to 2020 and was appointed Chair of the Children and Families Committee in 2021, a post he holds in 2025-2026.
Also serves on the Codes, Health, Rules and Ways and Means committees, the Task Force on New Americans and the Puerto Rican/Hispanic Task Force.

His Assembly biography lists laws he wrote, including a measure prohibiting the arrest and prosecution of children under 12 (excluding homicide), a replacement of anonymous reporting with confidential reporting to the State Central Register of Abuse and Maltreatment, and an extension of the statute of limitations for human-trafficking survivors to bring civil actions.
Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Jonathan Rinaldi, 87.7% to 11.8%.

priorities.text: Child care affordability and workforce support, sponsoring a statewide child care workforce pay-equity fund and a tax credit expanding employer-provided dependent-care benefits.
Child welfare system funding, including raising the state reimbursement rate for preventive child protective services and adjusting foster-care payment rates for cost of living.
Domestic violence protections, sponsoring a bill to create a new state crime of "coercive control" against a family or household member.

positions.summary: Sponsored multiple bills to fund child care affordability and pay equity for the child care workforce, including a permanent child care workforce pay-equity fund and expanded dependent-care tax credits for working families.

record.text: Sponsored A63-A, establishing a child and family well-being program and fund to distribute grants to nonprofit community-based providers; referred to the Children and Families Committee as of January 2026.
Sponsored A492-A, establishing the permanent child care workforce pay equity fund; referred to the Children and Families Committee.
Sponsored A598, expanding the employer-provided child care tax credit to cover in-home and backup dependent care; referred to the Ways and Means Committee.
Sponsored A679, creating the crime of "coercive control" against a family or household member as a class E felony; referred to the Codes Committee.
Sponsored A487, raising the state reimbursement rate for preventive child protective services from 65% to 75%; reported and referred to the Ways and Means Committee.

summary.text: David Kemp is running on the 4 Our Immigrants Party line for NY State Assembly District 28. Ballotpedia lists him among the Republican primary candidates who withdrew or were disqualified. Little other public information about him was found.

candidates.name: Jonathan Rinaldi
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary to Andrew Hevesi (11.8% of the vote); remains on the general-election ballot on the No Kings Party line.

summary.text: Jonathan Rinaldi is running on the No Kings Party line for NY State Assembly District 28 after losing the Democratic primary to incumbent Andrew Hevesi. He has run for several offices since 2023, including the City Council and this Assembly seat. He was arrested in June 2026 on fraud charges related to his 2025 City Council campaign; he is presumed innocent unless convicted.

background.text: Born in New York; Ballotpedia lists his profession as consultant. In a 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he described himself as having a background in architecture.
Was the Republican-line candidate for New York City Council District 24 in 2023, losing to incumbent James Gennaro with 23.4% of the vote.

Ran for Assembly District 28 in 2024 on the Republican, We the People and Truth lines, losing to Andrew Hevesi 58.6% to 41.1%; Ballotpedia also lists him as a Republican candidate for U.S. House in New York's 14th District in 2024 who withdrew before the primary.
Ran for City Council District 29 in 2025 as the Republican nominee, losing to incumbent Lynn Schulman with 27.3% of the vote.

In 2026, switched from the Republican to the Democratic Party to challenge Hevesi, according to the Queens Daily Eagle, and lost the June 23 Democratic primary; he remains on the November ballot on the No Kings Party line.

On June 24, 2026, he was arraigned on nearly 20 criminal counts that prosecutors said related to AI-generated campaign material in his 2025 City Council run. He told reporters he would not confirm or deny making the posts and that the case raised a First Amendment issue.

priorities.text: Community first; opposition to New York City's "City of Yes" zoning changes; a message that "it's not about the party, it's about policy."
Says he is passionate about public safety, healthcare, education, parental rights, and affordable housing, and describes his approach as practical policies and responsible budgeting.

positions.summary: Listed opposition to New York City's "City of Yes" zoning overhaul, which eased zoning rules to allow more housing citywide, as one of three key campaign messages.
positions.quote: No to the City of Yes

record.text: Arrested and arraigned on June 24, 2026 on nearly 20 counts of fraud tied to his 2025 New York City Council campaign against Lynn Schulman; prosecutors say he used AI-generated content, including fabricated endorsements attributed to public figures and fake news articles mimicking real outlets. The Queens Daily Eagle reported he also used AI-generated deepfake videos and images during both the 2025 City Council campaign and his 2026 Assembly primary campaign, though he was charged only over the 2025 campaign. He faces up to two years in prison if convicted.

researchNotes: David Kemp has no campaign website, Ballotpedia biography, or public statements on record (checked https://ballotpedia.org/David_Kemp, which shows no completed Candidate Connection survey); he withdrew from the Republican primary and is on the November ballot only via the 4 Our Immigrants Party line. Jonathan Rinaldi has not completed a 2026 Candidate Connection survey, but completed one in 2024 during a prior Assembly run for the same seat, cited for background and priorities; his 2026 candidacy is otherwise documented mainly through the June 2026 fraud arrest described above. Neither candidate has held office, so no record of official actions exists for them. Rinaldi's election history is from Ballotpedia; his biographical details beyond the 2024 survey are limited.
